Effective draft: 27 August 2026

Second Opinion is intended only for qualified pharmacy professionals as clinical decision support. It does not provide medical diagnosis, prescribe treatment, replace independent professional judgment, or support emergency response.

You are responsible for verifying all generated content, medicine classifications, doses, contraindications, interactions, red flags, and referrals before acting. Generated output may be incomplete, inaccurate, or unavailable.

You must obtain valid recording consent, protect patient confidentiality, comply with applicable healthcare, pharmacy, privacy, and workplace requirements, and avoid unnecessary identifiers. You must not use the service for unlawful, deceptive, discriminatory, or unsafe purposes.

The service is provided without a guarantee of clinical accuracy or uninterrupted availability. These terms may change; a new version requires renewed acknowledgement.

This draft is not legal advice and must be approved by qualified counsel before real-patient deployment.

Effective draft: 27 August 2026

Data processed may include account identifiers, symptom audio, transcripts, structured symptom details, assessments, pharmacist feedback, and technical diagnostics.

Data is used to authenticate users, transcribe recordings, generate decision-support assessments, display history, improve reliability, and meet security or legal obligations. Audio and derived health information may be sent to the configured backend and third-party AI providers.

Case data remains in app-private storage and configured backend storage until deleted or removed under the deployment retention policy. Using Delete in case history requests deletion of the associated case data.

Access must be limited to authorized personnel. Do not enter unnecessary direct identifiers. Questions, access requests, corrections, and deletion requests should be directed to the organization deploying this application.

This draft does not establish DPDP Act compliance by itself. The deploying organization must finalize notices, lawful basis, consent, retention, processor contracts, safeguards, grievance contacts, and incident procedures with qualified counsel.
